pages.text: "Move, slowpoke!" Moya shouted below the rocky hill. Kiki stood above, watching the distant grass. Moya wanted to climb up right now.
Kiki raised a paw. "Wait. The grass is moving. Let me watch a little—" "Scaredy-cat! Always telling me to wait!" Moya snapped. Kiki's head sank below their shoulders.
Kiki climbed down and disappeared into the burrow. Alone on the rock, Moya wasn't having fun. "Why did Kiki leave?"
Bored, Moya shouted across the hill. "Hey!" The hill returned it. "Hey!" Moya's ears perked in surprise.
Mom approached. "The hill sends your words right back. Try a kind word." "Hello!" Moya called. "Hello!" came back. "Kind words come back as kind words!"

Mom nuzzled Moya's neck. "Words are like echoes. Kind words, kind echoes. Sharp words, sharp echoes." Moya lowered their head. "That's why Kiki left..." Mom whispered, "Try 'Let's look together' instead of 'Move.'"
Moya ran to the burrow. "Sorry about before, Kiki. You're the best lookout! Let's look together!" Kiki peeked out. "Really? Thank you!" Moya's neck straightened.
They stood together on the rock. Kiki checked the grass. "Just a bird. It's all right now!" Moya called, "Thank you, Kiki!" The hill echoed, "Thank you!" Kind words, kind echoes!
Now Moya knew the steps. "One, pause before speaking! Two, choose kind words! Three, thank you and sorry!" That evening, Kiki brought grass. Moya spoke first. "Thank you!"
Mom curled her neck around Moya. "See Kiki smiling at your kind words?" Kind words came back as kind words. Kind words, kind echoes!
